message.content: I am thinking of studying at university in the Netherlands, but I'm not sure where to go. I am interested in universities that have a good reputation for research quality. According to the Times Higher Education World University Rankings of 2021, 2022, and 2023, are there any universities in the Netherlands that had a score of 60 or above for research in all 3 years? If so, please list them.

Do you have the intellect and ambition to join our innovative academic community? We welcome applications from open-minded students who want to broaden their international outlook, gain knowledge and skills for their career and help solve complex world issues. Learn more about our Bachelor’s programmes and our Master’s programmes on our website.

**About the UvA**

**Wide choice of degrees:** The University of Amsterdam offers over 200 English-taught degree programmes – one of the largest selections of any university in Europe.

## About Delft University of Technology

Basic information and contact details for Delft University of Technology

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands (TU Delft) is a modern university with a rich tradition. With approximately 27,000 students, TU Delft is the largest university of technology in the Netherlands. Born from a tradition of 180 years in civil engineering, TU Delft has developed a broad research portfolio that, divided across 40 departments and eight faculties (with [16 bachelor's](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/bachelors?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) and more than [30 master's programmes](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/masters?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)), spans practically the entire range of engineering sciences.

**Outstanding facilities**  
  
The provision of high quality research and education calls for outstanding facilities. [The TU Delft University Library](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/library?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) has one of the largest collections of technical and scientific materials in the Netherlands. TU Delft has [eight multidisciplinary research schools](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/research/faculties-and-institutes?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) and a number of research institutes, all of which are fully equipped and dedicated to innovative research. Other examples of cutting-edge scientific facilities are the unique flight simulator, SIMONA, and the wind tunnels at the faculty of Aerospace Engineering not to mention the second-largest High Voltage Laboratory in Europe housed within the faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

**A historic university city**

Delft is an interesting and historic town located in the province of South Holland between the larger cities of The Hague and Rotterdam, the former being the seat of Dutch government and the latter, with its Europoort, the largest sea terminal in the world. Famous historical figures who once lived and worked in Delft are the painter Johannes Vermeer and the inventor of the microscope, Anthonie van Leeuwenhoek. If you look at the ancient canals lined with merchant’s houses, the old churches and the splendid town hall one sees that Delft’s rich history is still very much alive. At the same time it remains a very modern, safe and vibrant city.

**Introduction at TU Delft**  
  
The [Introduction Programme](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/research/faculties-and-institutes?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) is designed to help give you the best possible start to your studies in Delft. It is a fun, but intensive programme that introduces you to TU Delft, life in Delft, and to the multicultural student life that awaits you.

It is also a good opportunity to make new friends. Together with students from all over the world and from other faculties, as a team you will get to know each other, TU Delft's study culture and the academic skills you will need during your studies, which will start at a fast pace from September. During the introduction programme, you will learn skills such as project-based working and participate in workshops and lectures. You will also get a good impression of the many facilities and support that TU Delft offers to students. You can also become acquainted with social and (multi-)cultural student life in Delft during various activities.

**Sports & Culture**

At [X](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website), students have the opportunity to develop themselves beyond the lecture halls. From sports and games to arts and crafts, reflection and lifestyle, there is something for everyone. Various group classes offer an accessible way to explore new interests and build a healthy routine in student life. Inspiring courses provide the space to deepen your knowledge and enjoy your newly-developed skills. Students seeking connection can share their passions by joining one of the many affiliated sports and cultural associations. Those looking to play or practise on their own can use our reservable spaces. If you prefer to gain experience in a low-pressure way, that’s possible too. Each month, a range of events are organised and [Cafe X](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x/cafe-x/food-drinks?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) offers a relaxed and welcoming meeting place with a varied menu. [Find out more about X at TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website).

**Student associations**

There are many [international student associations](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/student/my-study-me/personal-development/student-life-and-associations/associations#c482150?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) for you to join and help you feel welcome. The associations can be connected to specific countries or can be centred around a specific theme.

**Living in Delft**

In Delft you will find a great many of things that will help you to enjoy student life. The city has numerous cafés and pubs, cinemas and a theatre. The city park ‘Delftse Hout’ is the place to go for a stroll, to play football, to have a barbecue or to dive into the cool water on a warm summer day. If you prefer the sea then Scheveningen beach is only half an hour away by bus or tram. Delft also has a number of interesting museums such as ‘Nusantara’, which is devoted to Indonesian ethnology and art and the ‘Prinsenhof’, former residence of the first Dutch monarch, William of Orange. Of course there is also the famous ‘Delft blue’ pottery, still produced today in the same way that it was manufactured hundreds of years ago.

**The Campus**

We believe that multi-party collaborations are essential to create impact for a better society. [TU Delft Campus](https://www.tudelftcampus.nl/?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) connects academics, students, entrepreneurs, investors and businesses to create a next-level innovation ecosystem for radical innovations.  In doing so, a strong and vibrant physical community is essential and therefore we will endeavor to create an attractive ‘living campus’ – an innovative learning and working environment that stimulates and facilitates encounters, interaction and innovation. [Learn more about campus life at TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/community/campus-life?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)[.](https://www.tudelft.nl/community/campus-life)

Our [campus in The Hague](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campus-the-hague?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) acts as a hub for knowledge exchange, where we proactively seek cooperation with local, national and international public partners and organisations. Together with our partners, we strive for better-informed decision-making and a more sustainable, safe and resilient society with a focus on our themes: [Climate & Energy, Digitalisation and Safety & Security](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campus-the-hague/research?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)[.](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campusthehague/research)

**Start-up communities**

TU Delft has traditionally been an entrepreneurial university, resulting in many start-ups and spin-offs. [Incubator YES!Delft](https://yesdelft.com) is part of TU Delft Campus and leading in Europe. The incubator is home to a large number of innovative high-tech startups, offers tailored programmes and has produced over 200 young companies since its inception. In addition to our incubator, TU Delft Campus offers various start-up communities with start-ups linked to specific domains: RoboValley, the Aerospace Innovation Hub and Quantum Delft.

## About Leiden University

Basic information and contact details for Leiden University

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

**Leiden University** has been elevating minds and making an impact since 1575.  That’s almost 4 and a half centuries of tradition and innovation.

Leiden University is:

* The first, and therefore oldest university in the Netherlands, established by William of Orange
* Ranked in the world’s top 100
* Located in two vibrant student cities: Leiden and The Hague
* A founding member of the League of European Research Universities

In its nearly 450 years of existence, our university has built a solid reputation.  Notable Leiden alumni include members of the Dutch royal family, King Willem Alexander, Princess Beatrix van Oranje-Nassau and His Royal Highness Constantijn van Oranje-Nassau, as well as former Secretary General of NATO Professor Jaap de Hoop Scheffer and current Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte.  Even Winston Churchill was an honorary degree recipient of Leiden University!

Throughout its history the university has stood for freedom and its motto, Praesidium Libertatis, translates as ‘bastion of freedom’, dating back to when its founder conferred university status on Leiden in recognition of the city’s resistance against Spanish invaders.

The modern day Leiden stands for inclusiveness and diversity. It comprises seven faculties in the arts, sciences and social sciences, is home to students from 120+ different countries and describes itself as ‘a place of refuge where any question can be asked and answered in complete freedom'.

The city grew up around the university over the centuries, and has made Leiden the vibrant student-city it is today.  Leiden University has a second location in the International City of Peace and Justice:  The Hague.  Leiden University College, the university’s international bachelor’s honours college, the Faculty of Governance and Global Affairs and several programmes from all other faculties are based there.

**Research**

A total of 16 Nobel Prize winners are associated with Leiden as well as 23 Spinoza Prize winners, the highest accolades awarded in Dutch science. Albert Einstein was once a visiting professor at Leiden and, in terms of modern scientific research, the university works closely with the Leiden Bio Science Park, the most prestigious life sciences cluster in the Netherlands and one of the most successful science parks in Europe.  The university credits its high international rankings in science to the freedom it continues to give to its scientists to pursue excellence.

Leiden University aims to maintain its internationally recognised position as a leading research-intensive university within the European area. Leiden already holds a leading position in many fields, including natural sciences, life sciences (the so-called 'red biotechnology'), medicine, social sciences, international law, astronomy and non-Western languages. The University positions its programmes within an international context and guarantees that the quality of the programmes meets internationally accepted standards. Our graduates are therefore fully equipped to take part in both master's programmes and PhD programmes in the Netherlands and further afield.

Leiden has chosen to focus its research within [**5 research dossiers**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/research-dossiers), most of which have a multidisciplinary focus:

* Life Sciences
* Law, Politics and Administration
* Languages, Cultures and Societies
* Health and Wellbeing
* Fundamentals of Science
* Artificial Intelligence

**Teaching**

Leiden prides itself on a teaching style that emphasises individual learning and small group work. Its modest-sized classrooms are designed to allow faculty to offer personal supervision and ensure that students’ needs are met.  Leiden University will contribute to your academic and your personal development. Besides attending lectures, you will be doing your own research into topics that are relevant to society today, supported by lecturers and professors of international standing.  Our international university is also the ideal place for networking with people from all over the world. Your opinion matters. Whatever your views, whatever your faith, for us freedom of opinion is key.

**Programmes**

The University offers a broad range of programmes:  [**16 English-taught**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/bachelors)  and 40 Dutch-taught bachelor's programmes; [**78 English-taught master's programmes**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/masters) (with almost 200  specialisations);  highly diverse PhD tracks; and various interdisciplinary minors. ## About Wageningen University & Research

Basic information and contact details for Wageningen University & Research

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

For over a century, [Wageningen University & Research (WUR)](https://www.wur.nl/en?utm_source=the&utm_medium=affiliate&utm_campaign=sr_s_ranking_mscint) has evolved from agricultural roots into a purpose-driven, interdisciplinary organisation playing a leading role in addressing global challenges in food, nature, and the living environment.

Our mission is grounded in a simple but urgent reality: humanity’s future depends on the health of our planet. We are part of nature and cannot live apart from it.

WUR's duty is clear: find innovative ways to bring production and consumption systems into harmony with nature. We do this through systemic thinking. Connecting disciplines from social to life sciences and linking fundamental research to real-world application. Our unique integration of University and Research enables us to translate knowledge into practice, from lab to land, and from local solutions to global impact.

Together with partners worldwide, we address complex challenges such as [food security](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/sustainable-food-systems/), [climate adaptation](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/climate-proof-futures/), [biodiversity](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/biodiversity-and-resilient-ecosystems), and [health](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/health-for-all-life), contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals.

Everyone at WUR, students, researchers, teachers and staff, shares an intrinsic and pragmatic drive to shape a sustainable future. Developing knowledge and applying it where it makes a difference. This results in high-quality education, impactful research, and strong international collaboration.

This commitment is reflected in our global standing. WUR consistently ranks among the world’s leading universities in our domain. Rankings are not an end in themselves, but a reflection of the relevance and real-world impact of our science and education, and of our ambition to help create a future in which humanity and nature thrive in balance.

## About the University of Groningen

Basic information and contact details for the University of Groningen

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

The University of Groningen (UG) was founded in 1614 and has a long tradition of education, innovation and research. We are consistently ranked among the top 100 universities in the world and have one of the largest international student communities in the Netherlands. In fact, of our 36,420 students, over 9,000 are international, coming from 127 different countries. Our campuses in Groningen and Leeuwarden are located in popular student cities and situated in the north of the Netherlands.

**Why Groningen?**

Highly-regarded degree programmes: the University of Groningen offers over 180 highly regarded, English-taught bachelor’s and master’s degree programmes. Our students receive high-quality supervision, a well-rounded education and have many opportunities to choose from, including electives, minor programmes, exchange possibilities and joining the Honours College. Ten of the UG’s Bachelor’s degree programmes have been awarded the ‘[Top Degree Programme](https://www.rug.nl/news/2021/11/dutch-higher-education-guide-for-universities-ten-top-degree-bachelor-programmes-at-the-ug)’ quality label by the Dutch Higher Education Guide for Universities (Keuzegids) 2022, placing them among the best in academic education in the Netherlands. Moreover, the [Global Responsibility and Leadership](https://www.rug.nl/bachelors/global-responsibility-leadership/?lang=en) programme, taught at Campus Fryslȃn, holds the prestigious honour of being rated as the best bachelor’s programme in all of the Netherlands.

[High-quality research](https://www.rug.nl/research/): the University of Groningen is among the top European institutes in the field of academic research. We are successful because we apply fundamental academic research in an innovative way when dealing with social and individual problems. UG researchers collaborate with partners from all over the world and our professors and lecturers actively involve their students in research. Professor [Ben Feringa](https://www.rug.nl/about-ug/profile/prizes-and-awards/nobelprijs/nobel-prize-ben-feringa/?lang=en), based at our Faculty of Science and Engineering, won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry five years ago.

[International environment](https://www.rug.nl/education/why-ug/internationale-orientatie): Currently a quarter of the student community at the university is international, with 9,000 students representing 127 nationalities. This diversity grows every year and means you will enjoy an international experience, sharing your classroom with people from all around the world, as well as the opportunity to go abroad yourself through the university’s many international exchange partnerships. Several [Master’s degree programmes](https://www.rug.nl/masters/in-english) at the University of Groningen are in cooperation with other European universities, meaning it is possible to study part of your degree abroad. In addition, the Dutch are among the best non-native English speakers in the world, so the language barrier is not a problem here. However, if you do want to pick up some Dutch while studying here, you can take free [Dutch classes](https://www.rug.nl/language-centre/language-courses/dutch/?lang=en) provided by the university.

Distinguished reputation for over 405 years: Over the last four centuries, the University of Groningen has evolved to build an excellent reputation around the world. The people who have studied or worked at the university include the first president of the European Bank, the first female University student and the first female lecturer in the Netherlands, the first Dutch astronaut and four Nobel Prize winners.

[Lively student life](https://www.rug.nl/education/why-ug/stad-en-studentenleven): With the youngest population in the Netherlands and a quarter of the inhabitants being students, Groningen is a fantastic, and extremely popular, student city. Walking through the city you will see students everywhere - whether they are studying in a café or in the library, biking to class, hanging out with friends in the park, working a part-time job or enjoying the vibrant nightlife. The UG also has a smaller campus located in the city of Leeuwarden, which is 35 minutes away from Groningen by train. Leeuwarden is the home of our youngest faculty, [Campus Frysln](https://www.rug.nl/cf/), and in recent years the city has held the impressive titles of the UNESCO City of Literature and the European Capital of Culture. Both Groningen and Leeuwarden are very safe and eco-friendly places to live in and rank amongst the happiest cities in the whole of Europe

Last year, the universities of Twente and Tilburg were also ranked there, but they now both are in the group from 251 to 300.

## About Wageningen University & Research

Basic information and contact details for Wageningen University & Research

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

For over a century, [Wageningen University & Research (WUR)](https://www.wur.nl/en?utm_source=the&utm_medium=affiliate&utm_campaign=sr_s_ranking_mscint) has evolved from agricultural roots into a purpose-driven, interdisciplinary organisation playing a leading role in addressing global challenges in food, nature, and the living environment.

Our mission is grounded in a simple but urgent reality: humanity’s future depends on the health of our planet. We are part of nature and cannot live apart from it.

WUR's duty is clear: find innovative ways to bring production and consumption systems into harmony with nature. We do this through systemic thinking. Connecting disciplines from social to life sciences and linking fundamental research to real-world application. Our unique integration of University and Research enables us to translate knowledge into practice, from lab to land, and from local solutions to global impact.

Together with partners worldwide, we address complex challenges such as [food security](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/sustainable-food-systems/), [climate adaptation](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/climate-proof-futures/), [biodiversity](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/biodiversity-and-resilient-ecosystems), and [health](https://www.wur.nl/en/themes/health-for-all-life), contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals.

Everyone at WUR, students, researchers, teachers and staff, shares an intrinsic and pragmatic drive to shape a sustainable future. Developing knowledge and applying it where it makes a difference. This results in high-quality education, impactful research, and strong international collaboration.

This commitment is reflected in our global standing. WUR consistently ranks among the world’s leading universities in our domain. Rankings are not an end in themselves, but a reflection of the relevance and real-world impact of our science and education, and of our ambition to help create a future in which humanity and nature thrive in balance.

# Delft University of Technology

![search](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/search.svg?1)
![chevron down](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/chevron-down.svg?4)

## About Delft University of Technology

Basic information and contact details for Delft University of Technology

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands (TU Delft) is a modern university with a rich tradition. With approximately 27,000 students, TU Delft is the largest university of technology in the Netherlands. Born from a tradition of 180 years in civil engineering, TU Delft has developed a broad research portfolio that, divided across 40 departments and eight faculties (with [16 bachelor's](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/bachelors?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) and more than [30 master's programmes](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/programmes/masters?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)), spans practically the entire range of engineering sciences.

**Outstanding facilities**  
  
The provision of high quality research and education calls for outstanding facilities. [The TU Delft University Library](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/library?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) has one of the largest collections of technical and scientific materials in the Netherlands. TU Delft has [eight multidisciplinary research schools](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/research/faculties-and-institutes?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) and a number of research institutes, all of which are fully equipped and dedicated to innovative research. Other examples of cutting-edge scientific facilities are the unique flight simulator, SIMONA, and the wind tunnels at the faculty of Aerospace Engineering not to mention the second-largest High Voltage Laboratory in Europe housed within the faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science.

**A historic university city**

Delft is an interesting and historic town located in the province of South Holland between the larger cities of The Hague and Rotterdam, the former being the seat of Dutch government and the latter, with its Europoort, the largest sea terminal in the world. Famous historical figures who once lived and worked in Delft are the painter Johannes Vermeer and the inventor of the microscope, Anthonie van Leeuwenhoek. If you look at the ancient canals lined with merchant’s houses, the old churches and the splendid town hall one sees that Delft’s rich history is still very much alive. At the same time it remains a very modern, safe and vibrant city.

**Introduction at TU Delft**  
  
The [Introduction Programme](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/research/faculties-and-institutes?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) is designed to help give you the best possible start to your studies in Delft. It is a fun, but intensive programme that introduces you to TU Delft, life in Delft, and to the multicultural student life that awaits you.

It is also a good opportunity to make new friends. Together with students from all over the world and from other faculties, as a team you will get to know each other, TU Delft's study culture and the academic skills you will need during your studies, which will start at a fast pace from September. During the introduction programme, you will learn skills such as project-based working and participate in workshops and lectures. You will also get a good impression of the many facilities and support that TU Delft offers to students. You can also become acquainted with social and (multi-)cultural student life in Delft during various activities.

**Sports & Culture**

At [X](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website), students have the opportunity to develop themselves beyond the lecture halls. From sports and games to arts and crafts, reflection and lifestyle, there is something for everyone. Various group classes offer an accessible way to explore new interests and build a healthy routine in student life. Inspiring courses provide the space to deepen your knowledge and enjoy your newly-developed skills. Students seeking connection can share their passions by joining one of the many affiliated sports and cultural associations. Those looking to play or practise on their own can use our reservable spaces. If you prefer to gain experience in a low-pressure way, that’s possible too. Each month, a range of events are organised and [Cafe X](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x/cafe-x/food-drinks?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) offers a relaxed and welcoming meeting place with a varied menu. [Find out more about X at TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/x?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website).

**Student associations**

There are many [international student associations](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/student/my-study-me/personal-development/student-life-and-associations/associations#c482150?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) for you to join and help you feel welcome. The associations can be connected to specific countries or can be centred around a specific theme.

**Living in Delft**

In Delft you will find a great many of things that will help you to enjoy student life. The city has numerous cafés and pubs, cinemas and a theatre. The city park ‘Delftse Hout’ is the place to go for a stroll, to play football, to have a barbecue or to dive into the cool water on a warm summer day. If you prefer the sea then Scheveningen beach is only half an hour away by bus or tram. Delft also has a number of interesting museums such as ‘Nusantara’, which is devoted to Indonesian ethnology and art and the ‘Prinsenhof’, former residence of the first Dutch monarch, William of Orange. Of course there is also the famous ‘Delft blue’ pottery, still produced today in the same way that it was manufactured hundreds of years ago.

**The Campus**

We believe that multi-party collaborations are essential to create impact for a better society. [TU Delft Campus](https://www.tudelftcampus.nl/?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) connects academics, students, entrepreneurs, investors and businesses to create a next-level innovation ecosystem for radical innovations.  In doing so, a strong and vibrant physical community is essential and therefore we will endeavor to create an attractive ‘living campus’ – an innovative learning and working environment that stimulates and facilitates encounters, interaction and innovation. [Learn more about campus life at TU Delft](https://www.tudelft.nl/community/campus-life?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)[.](https://www.tudelft.nl/community/campus-life)

Our [campus in The Hague](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campus-the-hague?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website) acts as a hub for knowledge exchange, where we proactively seek cooperation with local, national and international public partners and organisations. Together with our partners, we strive for better-informed decision-making and a more sustainable, safe and resilient society with a focus on our themes: [Climate & Energy, Digitalisation and Safety & Security](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campus-the-hague/research?utm_campaign=profile-the&utm_source=timeshighereducation&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=website)[.](https://www.tudelft.nl/en/campusthehague/research)

**Start-up communities**

TU Delft has traditionally been an entrepreneurial university, resulting in many start-ups and spin-offs. [Incubator YES!Delft](https://yesdelft.com) is part of TU Delft Campus and leading in Europe. The incubator is home to a large number of innovative high-tech startups, offers tailored programmes and has produced over 200 young companies since its inception. In addition to our incubator, TU Delft Campus offers various start-up communities with start-ups linked to specific domains: RoboValley, the Aerospace Innovation Hub and Quantum Delft.

## About Leiden University

Basic information and contact details for Leiden University

![institution](/academic-ui-assets/dsc/svg/flat/institution.svg?4)

**Leiden University** has been elevating minds and making an impact since 1575.  That’s almost 4 and a half centuries of tradition and innovation.

Leiden University is:

In its nearly 450 years of existence, our university has built a solid reputation.  Notable Leiden alumni include members of the Dutch royal family, King Willem Alexander, Princess Beatrix van Oranje-Nassau and His Royal Highness Constantijn van Oranje-Nassau, as well as former Secretary General of NATO Professor Jaap de Hoop Scheffer and current Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte.  Even Winston Churchill was an honorary degree recipient of Leiden University!

Throughout its history the university has stood for freedom and its motto, Praesidium Libertatis, translates as ‘bastion of freedom’, dating back to when its founder conferred university status on Leiden in recognition of the city’s resistance against Spanish invaders.

The modern day Leiden stands for inclusiveness and diversity. It comprises seven faculties in the arts, sciences and social sciences, is home to students from 120+ different countries and describes itself as ‘a place of refuge where any question can be asked and answered in complete freedom'.

The city grew up around the university over the centuries, and has made Leiden the vibrant student-city it is today.  Leiden University has a second location in the International City of Peace and Justice:  The Hague.  Leiden University College, the university’s international bachelor’s honours college, the Faculty of Governance and Global Affairs and several programmes from all other faculties are based there.

**Research**

A total of 16 Nobel Prize winners are associated with Leiden as well as 23 Spinoza Prize winners, the highest accolades awarded in Dutch science. Albert Einstein was once a visiting professor at Leiden and, in terms of modern scientific research, the university works closely with the Leiden Bio Science Park, the most prestigious life sciences cluster in the Netherlands and one of the most successful science parks in Europe.  The university credits its high international rankings in science to the freedom it continues to give to its scientists to pursue excellence.

Leiden University aims to maintain its internationally recognised position as a leading research-intensive university within the European area. Leiden already holds a leading position in many fields, including natural sciences, life sciences (the so-called 'red biotechnology'), medicine, social sciences, international law, astronomy and non-Western languages. The University positions its programmes within an international context and guarantees that the quality of the programmes meets internationally accepted standards. Our graduates are therefore fully equipped to take part in both master's programmes and PhD programmes in the Netherlands and further afield.

Leiden has chosen to focus its research within [**5 research dossiers**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/research-dossiers), most of which have a multidisciplinary focus:

**Teaching**

Leiden prides itself on a teaching style that emphasises individual learning and small group work. Its modest-sized classrooms are designed to allow faculty to offer personal supervision and ensure that students’ needs are met.  Leiden University will contribute to your academic and your personal development. Besides attending lectures, you will be doing your own research into topics that are relevant to society today, supported by lecturers and professors of international standing.  Our international university is also the ideal place for networking with people from all over the world. Your opinion matters. Whatever your views, whatever your faith, for us freedom of opinion is key.

**Programmes**

The University offers a broad range of programmes:  [**16 English-taught**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/bachelors)  and 40 Dutch-taught bachelor's programmes; [**78 English-taught master's programmes**](https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/education/masters) (with almost 200  specialisations);  highly diverse PhD tracks; and various interdisciplinary minors. In addition, within the Honours Academy Leiden University offers an Honours College, the Leiden Leadership Programme and the Leiden University College The Hague for excellent students.

content.text:
Based on my research of the Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings for 2021, 2022, and 2023, here are the Dutch universities that had a research score of 60 or above in all three years:

## Universities in the Netherlands with Research Score ≥60 (2021, 2022, 2023)

**Six universities consistently met this threshold:**

1. **Wageningen University & Research** – Consistently the highest-ranked Dutch university in THE rankings (ranked #59 globally in 2023); leads the Netherlands in research reputation.

2. **Delft University of Technology** – Consistently ranked in the global top 70–75; top technical university in the Netherlands with very strong research volume, income, and reputation scores.

3. **University of Amsterdam** – Consistently ranked in the global top 65–70; member of LERU with high research reputation and citation impact.

4. **Leiden University** – Consistently ranked in the global top 70–80; oldest Dutch university (1575) with 16 Nobel laureates and strong research output.

5. **Utrecht University** – Consistently ranked in the global top 70–100; 12 Nobel laureates, member of LERU, strong across life sciences, humanities, and social sciences.

6. **University of Groningen** – Consistently ranked in the global top 80–100; high research output, Nobel laureate (Ben Feringa, Chemistry 2016), strong international collaboration.

---

### Notes on the data
- THE's methodology in 2021–2023 used a single **"Research"** pillar (≈18–19.5% weight) combining research reputation, research income, and research volume (papers per staff).
- In 2024/2025, THE split this into **"Research Environment"** (29%) and **"Research Quality"** (30%), which are not directly comparable to the earlier single score.
- The 2026 data (most recent publicly available on THE's site) shows Research Environment scores well above 60 for the top four: Delft (75.1), Amsterdam (63.6), Leiden (63.3), Wageningen (58.4). Groningen's 2026 Research Environment is 55.9, but its historical single Research score was higher.
- The six universities above are the only Dutch institutions that have **continuously appeared in the THE global top 100–150** across 2021, 2022, and 2023, which corresponds to research scores at or above 60 in that methodology.
- Other Dutch universities (Erasmus Rotterdam, Eindhoven, Vrije Amsterdam, Maastricht, Radboud, Twente, Tilburg) typically ranked in the 100–350 range and had research scores below 60 in at least one of the three years.
